issues.failure_explanation: def:sigm_act defines 'sigmoidal' by the limits sigma(t) -> 1 as t -> +infinity and sigma(t) -> 0 as t -> -infinity. tanh(t) -> -1 as t -> -infinity, and arctan(t) -> -pi/2 (resp. +pi/2, not 1), so neither the hyperbolic tangent nor the arctangent is sigmoidal in the sense of the definition; only their affine rescalings (1+tanh)/2 and arctan/pi + 1/2 are. The sentence is a false mathematical assertion under the paper's own definition.

failure_location.quote: For examples, the logistic sigmoid function, the hyperbolic tangens and the arctangens are sigmoidial.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop tanh and arctan from the examples, or state the sigmoidal rescalings (1+tanh)/2 and arctan/pi + 1/2 instead.
issues.overall_effect: No theorem or proof is affected, since all approximation results merely require some bounded sigmoidal activation and the logistic function qualifies; the defect is the false example claim itself.
issues.title: tanh and arctan do not satisfy the paper's own sigmoidal definition
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence false claim with an immediate local correction and no mathematical loss; nothing in the paper's definitions, theorems, or advertised guarantees depends on tanh or arctan specifically.

issues.failure_explanation: X_N and Y_N are defined as linear spans of finitely many functions, i.e., finite-dimensional subspaces of X and Y. A nonzero subspace of a normed space is unbounded (it contains lambda*v for every scalar lambda), and compact subsets of a metric space are bounded; hence these spans are not compact. Only their bounded subsets are relatively compact.

failure_location.quote: which are the compact subsets of $\X$ and $\Y$, respectively.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'compact subsets' by 'finite-dimensional (hence closed) subspaces', or state that the bounded subsets of X_N and Y_N are relatively compact.
issues.overall_effect: The false compactness assertion is not used anywhere later: the basis expansion, the operator F_N^#, and cor:rate only need finite-dimensionality, closedness, and orthonormality. The defect is the false statement itself.
issues.title: Finite-dimensional spans X_N and Y_N are falsely called compact
issues.why_classification: Isolated false claim with a word-level local repair and no downstream dependence; no proof step, construction, or guarantee relies on compactness of these subspaces.

Note that $F_

o$, that is, $F_
o^\#|_{\X_
o} = F|_{\X_

where $P_{\no}$ is the orthonormal projector onto $\Y_\no$.

issues.failure_explanation: Since F is linear and uly^(l) = F ulx^(l), the operator F_N^# equals F P_N^X with P_N^X the orthoprojector onto X_N, so the exact defect is Fx - F_N^# x = F(I - P_N^X)x. Because F P_N^X x lies in Y_N, (I - P_N)Fx = (I - P_N)F(I - P_N^X)x, hence ||(I - P_N)Fx|| <= ||Fx - F_N^#x||: the quantity (I-P_N)F controls a projection of the error, not the error itself, i.e., the displayed inequality goes the wrong way. Bounding the x-dependent ||Fx - F_N^#x|| by nu_N := ||(I - P_N)F|| (with no factor ||x||) is false in general: with X = Y = R^2, F e1 = e1, F e2 = e1 + e2, X_N = span(e1) one gets ||F e2 - F_N^# e2|| = sqrt(2) while nu_N*||e2|| = 1. Additionally, 'nu_N converges to 0 when F is compact' presupposes that the increasing training spans X_N become dense in X, which is never assumed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term by ||Fx - F_N^#x|| = ||F(I - P_N^X)x|| <= nu_N ||x|| with nu_N := ||F(I - P_N^X)|| and add the standard assumption that the training spans become dense in X; for compact F the corrected nu_N still tends to 0, so the form of all subsequent rates is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The first term of the estimate eq:estimate is unsupported as stated; the bound rho_n <= nu_N + N q(N) r(N) and the explicit rate sqrt(nu_N + N q(N) r(N)) in th:linear inherit the error, as does the following remark on the importance of nu_N.
issues.title: Wrong projector bound for the defect F x - F_N^# x in the linear neural-operator estimate
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local replacement of the first error term plus a standard density hypothesis; the qualitative conclusion (nu_N -> 0 for compact F) and every advertised rate survive unchanged, and no new nontrivial lemma or reoptimization is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: With a_l := <x, ulx^(l)>, A_l its branch-net approximation (|a_l - A_l| <= q(N) by eq:qn) and b_l := uly^(l), B_l its trunk-net approximation (||b_l - B_l||_Y <= r(N) by eq:rn), one has a_l b_l - A_l B_l = (a_l - A_l) b_l + A_l (b_l - B_l), so summing over l gives only ||F_N^# x - F~_n[x]|| <= q(N) * sum_l ||uly^(l)|| + r(N) * sum_l |<x, ulx^(l)>| + N q(N) r(N). The claimed bound N q(N) r(N) would require the two approximation errors to multiply, which they do not; the dropped terms are linear in q and r and dominate the product for small q, r. With the paper's own choices q(N) = N^{-2} and r(N) = N_j^{-1/2} (eq:estNqr), the true contribution is of order N(N^{-2} + N_j^{-1/2}), not 1/(N sqrt(N_j)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the correct product-estimate bound, e.g. ||F_N^#x - F~_n[x]|| <= C(N q(N) + sqrt(N) r(N)) + N q(N) r(N) on bounded sets, propagate it into th:linear (rate sqrt(nu_N + N q(N) + sqrt(N) r(N))), and re-optimize N_j against N in the example (e.g. N_j much larger than N^2).
issues.overall_effect: The second term of eq:estimate, and hence the explicit convergence rate sqrt(nu_N + N q(N) r(N)) in th:linear, is wrong; the subsequent example's conclusion that this term is negligible, and the remark that it 'seems to be of less importance', fail as stated.
issues.title: Product bound N q(N) r(N) for the branch/trunk approximation error drops dominant linear terms
issues.why_classification: The abstract rate O(sqrt(delta) + sqrt(rho_n)) of th:linear survives, but the quantitative expression for rho_N and the negligibility claim must be weakened and the example re-optimized; this is a contained correction leaving a recognizably comparable result, hence more than minor but without major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: be a continuous operator with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology, and assume that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$.

The proof follow easily from the Rellich-Kondrachov theorem (see \cite[Theorem 6.2]{Ada75}), which states that the embedding $H^s(\Omega_\X) \hookrightarrow C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$ is compact for $s > \frac{m}{2}$, and from \cite[Theorem 4 \& Theorem 5]{TiaHon95}.

issues.failure_explanation: The approximating functionals and operators are finite combinations of point evaluations x -> x(s_l), hence continuous in the C(Ω̄)-topology; anything they approximate uniformly on dom(F) must be C-continuous on dom(F). Continuity in the H^s-topology together with compactness of dom(F) in C does not imply C-continuity: on Ω = (0,1), s = 1, take x_n(t) = sin(n pi t)/n and dom(F) = {x_n} ∪ {0}; the x_n are pairwise H^1-orthogonal with ||x_n||_{H^1} -> pi/sqrt(2), so every point of dom(F) is H^1-isolated and F(x_n) := 1, F(0) := 0 is continuous in the H^1-topology, while dom(F) is compact in C because x_n -> 0 uniformly. Any C-continuous approximant G satisfies G(x_n) -> G(0), which is incompatible with sup-error < 1/4, so the theorem's conclusion fails with all stated hypotheses satisfied. Rellich-Kondrachov only supplies compactness of the embedding and does not transfer continuity between the two topologies; the cited Theorems 4 & 5 of [TiaHon95] require continuity in the topology of the compact domain, an omitted hypothesis. th:operatorapx contains the same defective hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: be a continuous functional with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology, and suppose that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to continuity of F with respect to the C(Ω̄)-topology on dom(F), or require dom(F) to be compact in H^s (on an H^s-compact set the H^s- and C-topologies coincide); the Chen-Chen argument then applies verbatim, and the paper's applications still comply (the Darcy operator is Lipschitz from C to L^2 on {x >= nu}; the mollified sets used in th:l2 operator apx are H^s-compact for every s).
issues.overall_effect: th:functional apx and th:operatorapx are false as stated; the advertised extension of neural-operator universal approximation from continuous functions to Sobolev spaces (abstract; the stated goal of Section sec:basisrep) is not established, and the justification of the local approximation assumption eq:nun for Sobolev-space forward operators (e.g. the a-example treated in Section sec:basisrep) via th:operatorapx is unsupported as written.
issues.title: H^s-continuity on a merely C-compact domain does not suffice for universal approximation
issues.why_classification: The statements are false as written and the repair strengthens the hypotheses, a limited weakening: all applications and a recognizably comparable Sobolev-space approximation theorem survive without new proof architecture, but the originally claimed generality for arbitrary H^s-continuous operators on C-compact domains is withdrawn.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a function $\x \in L^2(\Omega_\X)$, which is extended by zero outside of $\Omega_\X \subseteq \R^m$
Let $\xdag > \nu > 0 \in H^2(0,1)$ satisfy the source condition in \autoref{de:source_a}.

issues.failure_explanation: The mollifier is defined via extension by zero outside Ω. The zero extension of x ∈ H^k(Ω) belongs to H^k(R^m) only if the relevant traces vanish (x ∈ H_0^k); otherwise the extension has a jump across ∂Ω and the L^2 mollification error is only of order xi^{1/2}: for Ω = (0,1) and x ≡ 1 ∈ H^2(0,1), one computes x_xi(0) = ∫_0^xi phi_xi = 1/2 and ||x_xi - x||_{L^2} = Theta(sqrt(xi)). Item (v) of le:molli is therefore false as stated, and in the c-example the solution x† satisfies x† >= nu > 0, so its boundary trace is at least nu and the claimed ||x†_xi - x†||_{L^2} = O(xi^2) is false (it is Theta(sqrt(xi))).

failure_location.quote: For all $s \leq k$ and $\x \in H^k(\Omega_\X)$, $$\norms{\x_\xi-\x}_{H^s} \leq C\xi^{k-s}\norms{\x}_{H^k} = \mathcal{O}(\xi^{k-s})\;.$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In def:mollifier replace the zero extension by an H^k-preserving extension operator (e.g., symmetric reflection or a Stein extension); then item (v) holds for x ∈ H^k(Ω), the c-example's O(xi^2) mollification error is valid, and the advertised rate O(sqrt(delta) + sqrt(rho_{n xi}) + xi) is restored.
issues.overall_effect: le:molli (v) is false under the paper's zero-extension definition; the unlabelled c-example in Section se:generalization loses its premise ||xdag_xi - xdag|| = O(xi^2), so the rate eq:xi degrades from O(sqrt(delta) + sqrt(rho_{n xi}) + xi) to O(sqrt(delta) + sqrt(rho_{n xi}) + xi^{1/4}) (the mollification error enters under a square root), and the following remark's O(xi^2) mollification bound is likewise undercut.
issues.title: Mollification rate O(xi^{k-s}) fails under the zero extension used in def:mollifier
issues.why_classification: The failure hits the main intended application (xdag >= nu > 0 is incompatible with H_0^2), so it is not a degenerate-case fix; however, swapping in a standard extension operator is a contained construction that fully restores the advertised rates without new global architecture or major loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it holds locally uniformly in a $L^2$-neighborhood of $\xdag$ that $$\norms{F[\x_\xi]-F[\x]}_{L^2} \leq c\norms{\x_\xi-\x}_{L^2} = \mathcal{O}(\xi^2)$$ for some constant $c$.

issues.failure_explanation: Fréchet differentiability of F yields only local Lipschitz continuity, and mollification convergence ||x - x_xi||_2 -> 0 (le:molli (iv)) holds pointwise, not uniformly over L^2-balls: for fixed xi > 0 the mollifier damps high-frequency components to zero, so sup_{||x - x*|| <= r} ||x - x_xi||_2 >= r(1 - o(1)) along high-frequency directions. The inference from Fréchet differentiability to a locally uniform bound ||F[x] - F[x_xi]|| < eps/2 on B_r(x*) is therefore invalid, and the theorem is false as stated: for F = id (Fréchet differentiable), sup over B_r(x*) of ||F[x] - F_n[x_xi]|| >= r - o(1) minus the (small) network error on the mollified compact set, which exceeds any eps < r. Consequently rho_{n xi} in eq:deeponeterror_l2 cannot in general be made <= eps.

failure_location.quote: From the Fr\`echet-differentiability of $F$, it follows that there exists a $\xi > 0$ such that the following holds locally uniformly within an $L^2(\Omega_\X)$-neighborhood $\mathcal{B}_{\tt r}(\x^*)$ with radius ${ \tt r} > 0$ of $\x^*$:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the theorem to uniform approximation on C-compact sets (e.g., H^2-bounded or mollified sets) or to the single point xdag ∈ H^2, and justify the c-example by the standard operator-perturbation estimate at the solution, ||F[xdag] - F_n[xdag_xi]|| <= C xi^2 + eps (after the extension repair of le:molli), combined with uniform approximation of F on the compact set of mollified competitors; the final rate O(sqrt(delta) + xi) survives this restructuring.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed locally uniform L^2-approximation of F by x -> F_n[x_xi] (eq:deeponeterror_l2) is unavailable in general; the unlabelled c-example's choice rho_{n xi} ~ delta and its rate eq:xi, and the subsequent remark's 'locally uniform in an L^2-neighborhood' O(xi^2) estimate, are unsupported as argued.
issues.title: Uniform-in-L^2 approximation of F by F_n[x_xi] does not follow from Fréchet differentiability and is false in general
issues.why_classification: The theorem's headline claim (uniform approximation over L^2-balls) must be abandoned, but a contained weakening plus a standard perturbation-at-the-solution argument recovers the advertised c-example rate, so the resolution is a limited weakening rather than new global architecture or major loss.
